0.long_answer: Neuromyotonia is a condition of peripheral nerve hyperexcitability that manifests as spontaneous muscle activity. One of its characteristic symptoms is the occurrence of brief, spontaneous contractions of individual motor units. These contractions are known as fasciculations. Fasciculations involve the random, involuntary activation of a single motor unit, as opposed to myokymia, which usually involves multiple motor units producing rippling movements. In neuromyotonia, the hyperexcitability of the peripheral nerves leads to these spontaneous discharges, making fasciculations a common feature of the condition.
